messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: spike in pod crashes (runtime-service) in us-west2 - 40% error rate, reason: CUDA_ILLEGAL_MEMORY_ACCESS per logs. Auto-created incident channel #inc-2162509876
Maya: seeing same, started ~08:12 UTC, prod-serving cluster us-west2. rolling restarts not helping.
Raj: pulling logs now. one pod shows stacktrace with misaligned address on kernel entry. dmesg snippet attached below.
Sasha: reassigning oncall. @oncall-bot ping Raj as current oncall.
oncall-bot: Handoff: Raj is now the on-call responder for this thread.
Raj: quick status: ~12 pods crashed in last 20m. memory usage on nodes normal, GPU mem okay per nvidia-smi, but kernel reports pagewalk failures. suspect a kernel/driver race not model OOM.
Kevin: can you paste the pod logs?
Raj: paste: ```
E tensorflow: cudaCheckStatus() failed: CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS
...
backtrace: runtime_infer.cu:kernel_launch+0x1b2
...
dmesg: NVRM: GPU at 0000:65:00.0: GPU has fallen off the bus
[ 12345.678901] BUG: unable to handle kernel NULL pointer dereference at 0000000000000020
[ 12345.678905] Code: Bad PC value.
```
Leah: NV driver rev is 530.41 on these nodes. Any recent infra changes?
Maya: we deployed model-serve v2.4.7 yesterday which enabled a new fused attention kernel when batch_size > 64. Could be related.
Oliver: confirm: all crashes line up with requests that had large batch sizes from the batching-service. We saw a traffic spike at 08:08.
Sasha: immediate mitigation options?
Raj: short-term: (1) disable fused kernel via env var SERVE_DISABLE_FUSED_ATTENTION=true, (2) move traffic to fallback model-variant (cpu-safe/quantized) in us-west2, (3) cordon problematic nodes for now.
Maya: applying env change to canary first. rolling restart canary pods now.
Kevin: I can flip routing for 10% traffic to fallback variant.
Leah: infra: isolating two nodes that produced the pagewalk logs. starting node drain (no-restart) and will repro on spare nodes.
incident-bot: ACTION CREATED: mitigation/fallback-route, assignee Kevin, due 20m.
Maya: can anyone reproduce locally with same model + batch pattern? I have a repro script. sharing: ```bash
python repro_batch.py --batch-size 128 --iterations 10 --model redwood/gptx-legacy
```
Oliver: I ran that on staging GPUs (530.41) and got a deterministic illegal memory access inside the fused attention after 3 iterations.
Raj: good. that pins it to fused attention kernel + driver combo. escalating to infra/driver team. @Leah can you open a support ticket with cloud vendor and attach dmesg + stack?
Leah: ticket opened: CLOUD-98765. added logs and repro steps. contacting driver-engineer assigned.
Sasha: customer impact? Any 5xxs observed at API layer?
Kevin: yes, customer-facing error rate jumped to 6% for text-generation in us-west2. Most requests either retried successfully or served by fallback but some timed out. flagging potential SLA blips.
Oliver: posting a short status update to status.redwood.io: degraded performance in us-west2 for text-generation.
Maya: after disabling fused kernel on canary, canary pods stable for ~6m with no crashes. starting rollout to remaining pods in the region.
Raj: rolling the env var to all runtime pods in us-west2 now.
Leah: nodes drained and repro attempted on one node with driver older/newer versions. vendor suggested a micro-patch to the driver resolves pointer validation. waiting ETA from vendor (1-2 hours).
incident-bot: UPDATE: mitigation/fallback-route completed by Kevin.
Sasha: good. once rollout finishes, we should monitor for 30m and then assess next steps (driver patch vs keep fused off).
Maya: telemetry shows error rate down to 0.7% after rollout and most traffic served normally.
Kevin: re-route back to standard model path progressively.
Raj: note for postmortem: root cause likely a race in fused attention kernel that triggers a misaligned access on particular batch shapes + driver/firmware combo. Action items: (1) revert fused kernel enablement until kernel is fixed, (2) add automated canary that runs high-batch shaped requests after deploy, (3) add guard in runtime to catch illegal access and fallback gracefully without pod crash.
Oliver: adding those to incident ticket and PR queue.
Leah: vendor provided provisional driver build (530.43-patch1) to validate. planning to test on a pinned node in staging.
Maya: timeline: immediate mitigation complete, customer impact reduced. next up: validation of vendor patch and decide restore timeline.
incident-bot: RESOLVE: incident moved to "monitoring".
Sasha: thanks team. we'll keep this thread for postmortem notes. please add any logs or timelines to the incident doc. :thumbsup:
Raj: quick note for the postmortem: attach repro script, dmesg, pod logs, nvidia-smi outputs, and rollout timeline.
Leah: done. CLOUD-98765 updated with links.
Maya: closing handoff to product & infra for follow-up.
oncall-bot: Handoff complete. New owner: Infra Driver Eng.
